backlog.spec: Replace compute_max_radii with a correct version. The current code has a nested duplicate i/j loop that overwrites the loop variable i, and it scales radii pairwise in a way that does not guarantee feasibility. Compute each radius as the minimum of the border distances and, for each pair, enforce r_i + r_j <= d_ij by shrinking both radii proportionally only when violated, iterating until no pair is violated. Then verify feasibility with a tolerance check and shrink all radii by a factor of (1 - 1e-9) before returning.
backlog.title: Fix the broken radius computation

backlog.spec: Given fixed centers, compute the radii that maximise the sum exactly with scipy.optimize.linprog. Variables are r_1..r_26. Constraints: r_i <= x_i, r_i <= y_i, r_i <= 1 - x_i, r_i <= 1 - y_i, and r_i + r_j <= d_ij for every pair. Set bounds to r >= 0, maximise sum r by minimising -sum(r), and subtract a 1e-9 safety margin from the returned radii.
backlog.title: LP-optimal radii for fixed centers

backlog.spec: Optimise the 78 variables (26 centers and 26 radii) jointly with scipy.optimize.minimize using method SLSQP. The objective is minus the sum of radii. Constraints are inequalities: x_i - r_i >= 0, 1 - x_i - r_i >= 0, the same for y, and (x_i - x_j)^2 + (y_i - y_j)^2 - (r_i + r_j)^2 >= 0 for all pairs. Start from a feasible initial packing, supply analytic Jacobians for speed, and set maxiter around 500.
backlog.title: Joint SLSQP over centers and radii

backlog.spec: Minimise an energy over centers and radii with L-BFGS-B. The energy is minus the sum of radii plus a quadratic penalty mu times the squared overlap on each pair and each border violation. Run a sequence of solves with mu increasing geometrically, for example 10 to 1e6, warm-starting each solve from the previous result. After the last solve, repair feasibility with the LP radii step and shrink slightly.
backlog.title: Penalty relaxation with increasing stiffness

backlog.spec: Generate many random initial configurations of 26 centers using numpy.random.default_rng with a fixed seed such as 12345. For each, run the penalty-plus-LP local optimiser. Keep the packing with the largest valid sum of radii. Use a loop budget chosen so the total runtime stays under about 200 seconds, checking time.perf_counter.
backlog.title: Multi-start with a fixed seed

backlog.spec: Keep the current best packing. Repeat: perturb a random subset of 2 to 4 centers by Gaussian noise with standard deviation 0.05, clip them into the square, re-optimise with the local solver, and accept the new packing if its valid sum of radii is higher (Metropolis acceptance at a small temperature is allowed). Use a fixed seed and stop at a time limit of about 200 seconds.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from the best packing

backlog.spec: Run simulated annealing over the 26 center coordinates. At each step move one random center by a Gaussian step whose scale shrinks geometrically from 0.1 to 0.001. Score each state by the LP-optimal sum of radii for those centers. Accept worse moves with probability exp(delta/T), with T decaying geometrically. Track the best state and return its radii after a final safety shrink.
backlog.title: Simulated annealing on centers

backlog.spec: Simulate growing circles. Start all radii at a small value and in each step advance radii by a small increment, then resolve overlaps by moving centers apart along the line of centers in proportion to the overlap. Keep radii rates decreasing over time as the packing jams. Stop when no radius can grow, then polish with the LP radius step.
backlog.title: Lubachevsky-Stillinger style growth

backlog.spec: Build the packing one circle at a time. Maintain a candidate set of points on a fine grid, and place each new circle at the grid point with the largest distance to existing centers and borders. After each insertion, recompute all radii using the LP step and keep the packing. Do this for 26 circles, then run a final local optimisation on the completed packing.
backlog.title: Greedy hole-filling insertion

backlog.spec: Generate a hexagonal lattice with spacing chosen so that more than 26 points fall inside the unit square. Choose the 26 points that are best spread, by removing the points with the most close neighbours one at a time. Use the LP radius step on the chosen points. Try several lattice orientations and offsets, and keep the best sum of radii.
backlog.title: Hexagonal lattice clipped to the square

backlog.spec: Seed the centers with a hand-chosen structure: four circles near the corners, a few along each edge, and the rest in one or two interior rings of decreasing size. Put larger initial nominal radii at the centre and smaller ones at the edges. Then hand the seed to the local optimiser. This is a structured start, not a fixed final answer.
backlog.title: Ring and corner seeded initialisation

backlog.spec: Initialise the radii with a profile that is largest near the square's centre and smallest near the edges, for example r_i proportional to a decreasing function of distance from (0.5, 0.5). Place centers on a jittered grid. Feed the profile as the starting point into the joint optimiser so that the optimiser begins in a region where large circles sit in the middle.
backlog.title: Graded size profile initialisation

backlog.spec: Impose a symmetry to reduce the search space. Optimise only the free centers, and mirror each one across the diagonal y = x, or across the vertical line x = 0.5, to get the rest. If an odd number of circles is needed, place one circle on the symmetry axis. Optimise the reduced variables with the penalty solver, then unfold, run a final unconstrained polish, and take whichever is better.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric search space

backlog.spec: Restrict the packing to 180-degree rotational symmetry about (0.5, 0.5). Use 13 free centers and their mirror images at (1-x, 1-y), with the centre of the square reserved for one circle or left empty. Optimise the 13 free centers and the radii of the paired circles with the LP step, then run an unconstrained polish on all 26 circles.
backlog.title: Rotational 180-degree symmetry

backlog.spec: Iterate on the current best packing. Find the circle with the smallest radius, remove it, and reinsert it at the largest empty region found on a grid. Re-optimise all centers with the local solver and keep the result if it improves the sum. Repeat for a fixed number of rounds or until the time limit, using a fixed seed.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert the smallest circle

backlog.spec: Replace the hard penalty with a smooth energy using softplus of the overlap, with temperature beta that is increased over iterations. Minimise it with a hand-written Adam loop (beta1 0.9, beta2 0.999, learning rate decaying from 0.01 to 1e-4) using analytic gradients. Keep radii as variables and add minus their sum to the energy. Finish with the LP radius polish.
backlog.title: Adam on a softplus overlap energy

backlog.spec: Speed up the local solver by computing all pairwise distances and overlaps with numpy broadcasting on 26 by 26 arrays instead of Python loops. Provide analytic gradients for the penalty energy with respect to centers and radii. This lets the solver run many more iterations inside the time budget, which matters more than any single model change.
backlog.title: Vectorised analytic gradients

backlog.spec: During the penalty optimisation, add decaying Gaussian noise to the centers at each restart, with the noise standard deviation falling geometrically from 0.05 to 1e-4. This is a regulariser that helps escape poor local optima. After each noisy restart, run the local solver to convergence, keep the best packing found, and polish it with the LP step.
backlog.title: Gaussian jitter annealing of centers

backlog.spec: Use a force-directed relaxation in which each pair of circles repels with a force that scales with the sum of their radii, and border circles are pushed away from the walls. Iterate with a damping factor that decreases over time. After relaxation, compute the LP-optimal radii and keep the result. This spreads the circles so that the sum of radii can grow.
backlog.title: Repulsion with radius-weighted forces

backlog.spec: When solving the penalty problem, require each pair to be separated by a margin epsilon greater than zero, for example 1e-4, and each circle to be at least epsilon from the walls. This guarantees the final packing is strictly feasible in double precision. Set epsilon to decay toward zero as the solver converges, then do a final LP radius step with zero margin and a 1e-12 relative shrink.
backlog.title: Clearance margin regularisation

backlog.spec: Run the local optimiser on a modified objective in which each radius is weighted by a random factor drawn from a fixed-seed distribution, for example uniform between 0.8 and 1.2. Different weightings push the packing toward different size distributions. Evaluate each resulting packing by the true unweighted sum of its radii, and keep the best one.
backlog.title: Objective weight randomisation

backlog.spec: Build a square-grid initialisation with 26 points that is slightly denser than needed, randomly drop 0 to 6 points with a fixed seed, then jitter the remaining centers. Run the local solver on each start and keep the best valid packing. Vary the jitter amplitude across restarts from 0.01 to 0.1 to span different basins.
backlog.title: Random restarts from perturbed lattice

backlog.spec: Maximise the sum of radii subject to the containment and non-overlap inequalities using a log-barrier method. For a sequence of barrier weights t increasing geometrically, minimise minus the sum of radii minus (1/t) times the sum of logs of all slack values with L-BFGS-B or Newton steps. Start from a feasible packing and stop when the duality gap is tiny. Then do the final shrink.
backlog.title: Log-barrier interior-point method

backlog.spec: First optimise centers under the constraint that all radii are equal to a single variable s, maximising s with 26 circles. Use this equal-radius packing as the warm start for a second phase in which all 26 radii are free and the sum of radii is maximised with the joint SLSQP step. Keep the better of the two phases if the second phase fails.
backlog.title: Two-phase equal-then-free radii

backlog.spec: Run the local solver with loose convergence tolerances, for example 1e-3 on gradients, for an initial stage. Then tighten to 1e-9 over several stages, each warm-started from the last. This saves time in the early stages where exact convergence is wasteful, which leaves more budget for global exploration.
backlog.title: Coarse-to-fine tolerance schedule

backlog.spec: Wrap the whole optimisation in a loop that checks time.perf_counter against a budget of about 200 seconds and stops early. Track the best valid packing and its sum throughout. Before returning, re-verify all constraints in double precision, and if the best packing is invalid, fall back to the best valid one found so far. This guarantees a valid output inside the harness limit.
backlog.title: Time-budgeted restart loop with best-so-far tracking

backlog.spec: Starting from the best packing, run repeated perturbation-and-reoptimise rounds in which the perturbation magnitude decays from 0.1 to 0.002 over the rounds. Early rounds explore broadly and late rounds refine. Accept only improvements. Use a fixed seed so the result is reproducible.
backlog.title: Shrinking perturbation schedule

backlog.spec: Run a batch of, say, 40 short local optimisations from different seeds, each with a small iteration cap. Rank them by valid sum of radii and continue only the top 5 to full convergence. This successive-halving scheme spends most of the budget on the most promising basins. Everything uses a fixed seed.
backlog.title: Parallel-style batch of seeds with early pruning

backlog.spec: Before returning, recompute every border and pairwise constraint in double precision using the returned centers and radii. Shrink all radii by the smallest multiplicative factor needed so that every constraint holds with zero tolerance, for example by dividing by one plus the maximum violation plus 1e-12. Report the sum of the final radii so that the reported total matches the returned radii exactly.
backlog.title: Rounded-precision final validation

backlog.spec: After the best packing is found, build its contact graph: pairs with (r_i + r_j) - d_ij < 1e-7 and borders with r_i - x_i (or the equivalent) < 1e-7. Treat these as equalities and solve the resulting square-ish nonlinear system for centres and radii with a few Newton or Gauss-Newton iterations (numpy least-squares on the Jacobian of the active constraints, using the LP dual or the SLSQP multipliers to decide which constraints to keep). Accept the refined solution only if _valid_packing passes and the sum improves; otherwise keep the current packing. This sharpens the tangencies that SLSQP leaves slightly slack.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton refinement of the final packing

backlog.spec: Instead of building 26 circles directly, optimise a packing of 27 circles (same _local_opt pipeline, starting from the seeded random or LS-growth start). Then drop the circle whose removal gives the largest resulting LP-optimal sum of radii (try all 27 removals, scoring each with _lp_radii on the remaining centres, and keep the best), and re-run _local_opt on the 26 remaining centres. Keep this as one more candidate start inside jitter_anneal_search, so it competes with the existing starts.
backlog.title: Remove-from-27 construction

backlog.spec: Maintain a small pool (about 6) of the best distinct packings found so far, keyed by sum of radii. Create a child by cutting each parent with a random line through the square and taking the circles on one side from parent A and the rest from parent B, adjusting the count to exactly 26 by dropping or adding random points, then run _local_opt on the child. Replace the worst pool member if the child is better and not a duplicate (sum within 1e-6). Use a fixed seed and run this in place of some jitter steps inside the restart loop.
backlog.title: Elite-pool recombination (genetic crossover)

backlog.spec: After the current best packing, try swapping the positions of every pair of circles with different radii (there are about 325 pairs). For each swap, keep the centres, exchange the two centres, and score the new layout with _lp_radii, which is cheap. Take the best swap if it improves the sum, then re-run _local_opt on it. Repeat until no swap improves or a time cap is reached. This explores discrete reassignments of big and small circles that continuous jitter does not reach.
backlog.title: Pairwise exchange local search scored by LP

backlog.spec: Replace the single monotone learning-rate decay in _adam_soft with a cosine-cycled schedule: run 3 to 4 cycles, each with lr decaying from 0.01 to 1e-4 and beta annealed from 20 to 2000 within the cycle. At the start of each new cycle, restart the Adam moment estimates and perturb the centres by a small Gaussian (sigma about 0.005). Keep the candidate from each cycle, and pass the best one through _lp_radii and _local_opt as the existing code does.
backlog.title: Cyclic-learning-rate Adam restarts on the softplus energy

backlog.spec: Add a sequential LP solver as an alternative local optimiser. At each step, linearise every pair constraint (r_i + r_j) <= d_ij and every border constraint around the current centres and radii, and solve a linprog problem in the step variables (dx, dy, dr) with a box trust region of radius delta. Maximise the sum of radii. Accept a step if the true (nonlinear) constraints are satisfied and the sum improves, and otherwise shrink delta; grow delta after successful steps. Run about 50 iterations from the best starting packing and feed the result into the existing candidate comparison in _local_opt.
backlog.title: Trust-region sequential linear programming

backlog.spec: Speed up the SLSQP stage in _local_opt by only including pair constraints for pairs whose centres are within a cutoff (for example, distance below sum of current radii plus 0.25). Build the pair list once at the start of each SLSQP call and rebuild it after each outer iteration if any circle moved more than 0.1. Pass this reduced pair set to the constraint function. Check after optimisation that all pairs are still valid with the full _valid_packing test, because pruned pairs could in principle overlap. The point is to allow more SLSQP iterations within the same time budget.
backlog.title: Neighbour-list truncated constraints for faster SLSQP

backlog.spec: In _adam_soft, replace the radius variable r with a squared variable r = s^2 (or a softplus of an unconstrained variable) so that the radii stay non-negative without clipping and the gradient flows through the reparametrisation (multiply the radius gradient by 2s, or by the sigmoid derivative). Remove the hard clip on radii and keep the clip only on centres. Compare the resulting sum to the clipped version inside _local_opt candidates, so the change can only help the final result.
backlog.title: Radius reparametrisation for the Adam energy

backlog.spec: Change the random initial centres used by _ls_growth and the jitter starts. Instead of sampling uniformly in (0.1, 0.9)^2, sample a fraction (about 40 percent) of the centres from a distribution concentrated near the four edges and corners (for example, a Beta(0.5, 0.5) draw on each coordinate), and the rest uniformly. Use the seeded rng so the result is repeatable. Run the existing pipeline on each start. This gives the optimiser starts that already have circles along the walls, where the best known packings usually place the smaller circles.
backlog.title: Boundary-weighted random starts

backlog.spec: Generate the initial 26 centres with a seeded low-discrepancy sequence instead of pseudo-random uniform draws. Implement a simple Halton or Sobol generator in numpy (van der Corput sequences in bases 2 and 3, mapped into [0.05, 0.95]^2), and use a random digit scramble from the seeded rng for each restart. Feed the resulting centres into _local_opt as one of the start candidates in jitter_anneal_search, and keep the other starts unchanged, so the search covers the square more evenly than a plain uniform draw.
backlog.title: Quasi-random Sobol-style initial centres

backlog.spec: Replace the jitter-anneal loop in jitter_anneal_search with a diagonal or full-covariance CMA-ES over the 52 centre coordinates (seeded, population about 12, sigma0 about 0.05). Each candidate's fitness is -sum(_lp_radii(c)), so the LP is the only evaluator and no SLSQP runs inside the loop. Keep the best 3 centre sets by LP sum, then run _local_opt once on the best to polish. Stop at the time budget and return the best packing seen, validated with _valid_packing.
backlog.title: CMA-ES over centres scored by LP radii

backlog.spec: Add a population-based stage before _local_opt: a seeded differential evolution (rand/1/bin, F=0.6, CR=0.9, population 40) over the 52 centre coordinates, clipped to [0,1]. Each individual is scored by -sum(_lp_radii(c)), which is cheap. Seed the population with the current best centres plus Gaussian perturbations and the lattice starts. After about 60 s, take the top 3 individuals into the existing _local_opt pipeline and keep the best result.
backlog.title: Differential evolution on centres with LP fitness

backlog.spec: Take the incumbent packing and compute its contact graph: pairs with radii sum within 1e-6 of distance, and circles touching a wall. Pick one active contact at random, remove it by nudging one endpoint away by about 0.01, and add a new contact by moving that circle to touch a different neighbour or wall. Re-run _local_opt on the modified centres, accept if the LP sum improves, and repeat for a fixed number of moves within the time budget. This is a combinatorial move, not a random jitter.
backlog.title: Contact-graph switching moves

backlog.spec: Add a start where circles are symmetric under reflection across the main diagonal (x,y) to (y,x). Sample 13 free centres with 26 coordinates, of which 13 are mirrored; the 26 points are free centres plus their mirrors, with any centre on the diagonal forced to be self-mirrored. Build the 26-point configuration, run _local_opt on it, and let the unconstrained _local_opt drop the symmetry. Add this start to the restart loop in run_packing as one of the seeds.
backlog.title: Diagonal-reflection symmetric start

backlog.spec: In _reinsert_polish, add a second move type alongside remove-and-reinsert. Pick a circle that touches a wall, slide it along that wall to a random position in [0,1] on that edge, and call _local_opt on the modified configuration. Alternate the two move types, accept only strict sum improvements under _valid_packing, and track the attempt counter so that both moves get equal time. This targets the edge arrangement that the interior-focused moves rarely reach.
backlog.title: Wall-slide relocation move

backlog.spec: After the existing reinsert polish, run scipy.optimize.minimize with method='trust-constr' on the joint variables (centres and radii) with the same pair and boundary constraints as _local_opt, using a fresh Jacobian from finite differences or the analytic form already used in _local_opt. Set maxiter to 200 and gtol to 1e-10. Compare the result with the current best using _lp_radii on its centres and keep whichever is larger, after _valid_packing. The method is a different constrained solver from SLSQP and may find small improvements SLSQP stops short of.
backlog.title: Trust-constr final polish

backlog.spec: Before the free-radius SLSQP in _local_opt, run an intermediate stage where circles are split into two size classes (the k smallest by current radius and the rest), with radii tied within each class. Optimise the centres and two class radii with SLSQP, then release the ties and run the free-radius SLSQP from that warm start. Choose k in {8,10,12} at random with a seeded generator, and keep the variant that gives the best LP sum. This is a schedule of constraint relaxation from fewer to more radius degrees of freedom.
backlog.title: Two-class radius tying before free SLSQP

backlog.spec: Add a perturbation move that keeps the centres fixed and perturbs only the radii: multiply each radius by a factor drawn uniformly from [0.9, 1.0] for a random 30 percent of circles, then re-solve the radii by _lp_radii on the unchanged centres. Use this as a cheap move inside jitter_anneal_search, interleaved every few steps with the centre-jitter move. The LP projects the perturbed radii back to the feasible maximum, so this explores different radius distributions on the same centres.
backlog.title: Radius-only basin hopping

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 1e-10 shrink in _lp_radii with an exact rescale. After the LP gives radii r, compute for every circle and constraint the slack: the wall slacks and the pair slacks dist minus r_i minus r_j. Find the smallest positive slack ratio and scale all radii by it, so the packing is exactly tight in double precision and still passes _valid_packing with zero tolerance. If the check fails, fall back to shrinking by 1e-12 and re-check. This recovers the tiny loss from the fixed margin.
backlog.title: Exact-feasibility radius rescale

backlog.spec: Run _adam_soft from several seeded starting points, each generated by _lattice_start with a different amplitude and seed, and also from the current best centres with Gaussian noise of scale 0.01. Keep the top 3 results by LP sum and pass each to _local_opt. Use a fixed seed sequence so runs are repeatable. Budget the total time so that the Adam stage uses at most about 60 percent of the search time.
backlog.title: Multi-start Adam with reseeded radii

backlog.spec: Add a move to _reinsert_polish that is distinct from remove-and-reinsert. Pick two adjacent small circles, delete them, and place one circle at their midpoint with the combined area-equivalent radius, scaled to stay inside the square. Then pick the largest circle and split it into two half-radius circles placed side by side along its longest free direction. Keep the candidate only if _local_opt returns a larger valid sum. This changes the size distribution, not only positions, so it can reach a different contact graph.
backlog.title: Merge-and-split move for circle sizes

backlog.spec: Before each _local_opt call inside jitter_anneal_search, run a few iterations of weighted Lloyd relaxation: compute the power (Laguerre) diagram of the current centres with weights r_i^2, clip each cell to the unit square, and move each centre a fraction (about 0.3) of the way toward its cell's weighted centroid. Use a seeded RNG for any tie-breaking. This spreads circles evenly by their size and gives SLSQP a better starting configuration than raw jitter.
backlog.title: Power-diagram Lloyd relaxation with radius weights

backlog.spec: Optimise the packing inside a virtual square of side L, starting with L = 1.25 and random centres. Every few iterations, shrink L toward 1.0 by a geometric factor while running a penalty-based relaxation (squared overlap plus boundary violation, weight increasing each step). Circles that remain overlapping after L reaches 1.0 are handled by the existing _local_opt. This is a container-shrink continuation, not a radius growth, and it lets the structure settle before the boundary becomes binding.
backlog.title: Container compression continuation

backlog.spec: Add a polishing routine for fixed target radii. Stack residuals: for each pair, min(0, d_ij - r_i - r_j), and for each boundary, min(0, x_i - r_i) and similar terms. Use scipy.optimize.least_squares with method 'lm' on centres, with radii set to the LP solution scaled by a target factor (about 1.001 of the current sum per radius). Repeat with the target increased by a small step while the residual norm stays near zero. Keep the last feasible configuration, then take the LP radii. This is a different solver family from SLSQP and the Adam energy.
backlog.title: Levenberg-Marquardt on squared overlap residuals

backlog.spec: Add a structured start that uses four rotated blocks. Split the square into four quadrants. In each quadrant, place a jittered triangular-lattice patch of about 6 or 7 circles, with each block rotated by 90 degrees relative to its neighbours in a pinwheel pattern, so the block boundaries interlock. Assign the counts so the total is exactly 26, then clip to the square. Feed this as the start argument to jitter_anneal_search for one of the restarts, with a fixed seed.
backlog.title: Pinwheel quadrant start

backlog.spec: Change the initial radii used by _adam_soft and by the LP stage. Sample a random permutation of 26 target radii from a power law r_k proportional to k^(-alpha), with alpha drawn from a seeded uniform in [0.3, 0.8], normalised so the largest target is 0.2. Assign the sorted targets to the circles by their current distance from the centre, so larger targets sit closer to the middle. Use these as the z initial radii before the Adam energy. This is a data prior on sizes, not on positions.
backlog.title: Power-law radius prior for initial sizes

backlog.spec: Replace the single Adam chain inside jitter_anneal_search with 4 replicas of _adam_soft at fixed, different softplus betas (for example 50, 200, 800, 3000). After every 100 iterations, attempt a swap between adjacent replicas with a Metropolis rule on the energy difference, using a seeded RNG. Keep the replica with the lowest beta as the output candidate to pass to _local_opt. The high-beta replicas explore, the low-beta ones refine, and swaps let basins propagate between temperatures.
backlog.title: Replica exchange over Adam softplus chains

backlog.spec: Add an optimizer stage after _local_opt. Set up an augmented Lagrangian on the joint variables (centres and radii) with the objective minus the sum of radii, and the pair and boundary constraints as equalities relaxed by multipliers. Each outer step minimises the augmented function with L-BFGS-B using analytic gradients, then updates the multipliers lambda = max(0, lambda + mu * g) and increases mu by a factor of 2 up to a cap. Stop after about 8 outer steps or 20 seconds. Keep the result only if _valid_packing passes and the LP-scored sum improves.
backlog.title: Augmented Lagrangian on pair contacts

backlog.spec: In _adam_soft, add stochastic gradient Langevin noise: after each Adam step, add Gaussian noise to the centre coordinates with standard deviation sqrt(2 * T_t * lr_t), where T_t decays geometrically from 1e-3 to 1e-7 across the iterations. Draw from a seeded numpy generator derived from the seed argument. The noise is small at the end, so the final iterations are a normal Adam descent. Pass the seed through jitter_anneal_search so each restart draws a different path.
backlog.title: Langevin noise injection into the Adam energy

backlog.spec: Add a structured start that places circles in horizontal rows rather than on a grid. Choose a row-count pattern from a fixed list, such as 5-5-5-5-6, 4-5-6-5-6, or 6-5-5-5-5, and distribute centres in each row at even horizontal spacing with a vertical offset that alternates by half a row for odd rows. Add a seeded jitter of about 0.02. Use this as the start argument for some restarts in run_packing, cycling through the patterns, so that different row counts are explored with the same downstream pipeline.
backlog.title: Row-count layout starts

backlog.spec: Replace the random or lattice starts in _ls_growth and _lattice_start with a seeded Bridson Poisson-disk sampler on [0.05, 0.95]^2. Use a minimum spacing of about 0.2 and draw candidate points in annuli around accepted points, rejecting any that fall within the spacing. Accept at most 26 points, and if the sampler stalls, lower the spacing by 5 percent and retry until 26 points are placed. Feed these centres to _local_opt as the start for every jitter-anneal restart with a different seed. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Poisson-disk initial centres

backlog.spec: Add a start generator that places the 26 centres on a Vogel (sunflower) spiral, using p_k = 0.5 + sqrt(k + 0.5) / sqrt(26 + 0.5) scaled and mapped into the unit square by a centred rescale to [0.1, 0.9]. Apply a seeded random rotation about the centre and a small seeded jitter of amplitude 0.02. Use it as the start for one restart in the run_packing loop (for example k % 5 == 4), leaving other restarts unchanged, and keep the best result as before.
backlog.title: Vogel spiral start with random rotation

backlog.spec: Add a new local optimiser that maximises a smooth surrogate of the minimum pairwise and border slack for fixed radii scaled to the current sum. Define the slack of each constraint as dist_ij - r_i - r_j and each border slack as the distance to the wall minus r_i. Minimise the negative log-sum-exp of the negated slacks with temperature t, using L-BFGS-B with analytic gradients over centres and radii jointly. Decrease t geometrically from 0.05 to 1e-4 over about 30 steps, warm-starting each step. Finish by calling the existing _lp_radii and the existing _valid_packing check, and add the result as a candidate in _local_opt.
backlog.title: Log-sum-exp smoothed max-min continuation

backlog.spec: In _local_opt, before the free-radii SLSQP, solve a sequence of problems that maximise sum(r_i^q) subject to the same pair and border constraints, with q stepping from 0.5 up to 1.0 in five equal steps. Each step is warm-started from the previous solution using SLSQP with analytic gradients for the power objective. Radii must stay positive, so use a lower bound of 1e-6 on r. The final q=1 solution is the seed for the existing SLSQP and LP candidates. Keep all existing candidates so the best packing is still chosen by LP sum.
backlog.title: Power-mean homotopy on the radii objective

backlog.spec: During the Adam softplus energy in _adam_soft, add a term -lambda * sum((r_i - mean(r))^2) to the objective, where lambda starts at 0.05 and decays linearly to zero over the iterations. This rewards a spread of circle sizes early and lets the optimiser move away from near-equal symmetric basins that the search keeps returning to. Compute its gradient analytically and add it to the radius gradient. After annealing, run the existing _lp_radii on the final centres so the radii are set exactly for the packing.
backlog.title: Radius-variance regulariser to escape symmetric basins

backlog.spec: Add a move that uses the LP dual values to choose which circle to relocate. After solving the LP in _lp_radii, read the dual values (marginals) of the pair and border constraints from the HiGHS result, and compute for each circle the sum of duals on constraints touching it. Circles with the smallest total dual weight are the least constrained. Pick one of the three least-constrained circles with a seeded random draw, move it to the grid point with the largest clearance (as in _reinsert_polish), and re-run _local_opt. Accept the result only if the LP sum strictly improves, and use this move alongside the existing remove-and-reinsert step.
backlog.title: Dual-guided relocation of loose circles

backlog.spec: Add a construction path that first optimises 25 circles with the existing jitter-anneal search (budget about 20 seconds, seeded). Then add a 26th circle at the grid point of a 61 by 61 grid with the largest clearance from the 25 existing circles and their radii, and call _local_opt on the 26 centres. Repeat the insertion for the best of three different 25-circle optima and keep the best valid 26-circle packing, which then enters the existing run_packing comparison. This is distinct from the remove-from-27 construction and from the smallest-circle reinsert step.
backlog.title: Add-to-25 insertion from a 25-circle optimum

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform Gaussian perturbation in jitter_anneal_search with a targeted one for part of the iterations. After each local optimisation, rank circles by radius. On a random half of the iterations, perturb only the four smallest circles with a Gaussian of sigma equal to the current schedule value times 5, leaving the others fixed at their positions, and call _local_opt on the result. On the other half, keep the existing uniform perturbation. Accept by the existing best-sum rule, and keep the same seeded generator so runs repeat exactly.
backlog.title: Targeted perturbation of the smallest circles

backlog.spec: Add an optimiser that sweeps the 26 centres in a seeded random order. For each centre, evaluate the LP sum (via _lp_radii) on a 1-D grid of 25 candidate positions along each of x and y, spanning a window of plus or minus 0.05 around the current point and clipped to [0, 1]. Move the centre to the best candidate if the LP sum increases. Repeat sweeps while the total gain exceeds 1e-6 and the time budget of 15 seconds is not used up. Run this on the best packing returned by the jitter-anneal search, before the reinsert polish stage, and keep the result only if the valid-packing check passes.
backlog.title: Cyclic coordinate line search on single centres

backlog.spec: Add a new stage after _local_opt. For the current centres, solve the radii LP (as in _lp_radii) and read the dual variables of the active pair and border constraints from res.ineqlin.marginals (HiGHS). The derivative of the LP optimum with respect to each centre coordinate is the sum over active constraints of dual times the partial derivative of the constraint right-hand side (pair distance d_ij w.r.t. x_i, y_i, etc.). Take a projected gradient ascent step on the centres (clipped to [0,1]^2, step size halved when the LP value falls), re-solve the LP, and stop after about 60 iterations or when the gain is below 1e-9. Keep the result only if the LP sum improves. Apply this to the best packing at the end of run_packing before the reinsert stage.
backlog.title: LP dual sensitivity gradient ascent on centres

backlog.spec: Define the smoothed objective F(c) = E[LP_sum(c + sigma*Z)] estimated with K=16 fixed Gaussian samples Z (common random numbers from a seeded generator), where LP_sum is the optimal sum of radii for fixed centres from _lp_radii. Estimate its gradient by central differences on the centre coordinates using the same samples, and run projected gradient ascent on the centres for about 40 steps with a step size that shrinks by half whenever F decreases. Start sigma at 0.02 and halve it every 10 steps down to 0.0005, so the search first explores broadly and then sharpens onto a nearby basin. Finish with a call to _local_opt on the final centres and keep whichever packing has the larger sum. Use the same seed for each run of jitter_anneal_search.
backlog.title: Randomised-smoothing gradient of the LP value

backlog.spec: Modify _reinsert_polish so that it keeps a tabu list of (circle index, grid cell) pairs that were tried recently and did not improve the sum. Each attempt removes the smallest circle as now, but it skips grid points within 0.04 of any tabu cell for that circle, so the search does not cycle among the same few relocations. The tabu entries expire after 12 attempts. Also allow an aspiration rule: a tabu move is accepted if it would beat the best sum found so far by more than 1e-6. Keep the same deadline logic and the same _valid_packing check.
backlog.title: Tabu memory for remove-and-reinsert moves

backlog.spec: Add a dictionary cache in jitter_anneal_search and _reinsert_polish keyed by a fingerprint of the converged packing. The fingerprint is built by rounding the sorted radii to 4 decimals together with the sorted list of contact pairs (pairs whose gap is below 1e-6), then hashed to a tuple. Before running _local_opt on a new candidate, compute its fingerprint from the start point's nearest local result only when it is cheap; more usefully, after each _local_opt call, if the fingerprint was already seen, do not count that candidate as new progress and instead perturb the best packing with a larger sigma (0.05) for the next step. Log the number of unique basins visited in a module-level counter. The change is intended to spend the time budget on new basins rather than on repeats of the same local optimum.
backlog.title: Fingerprint cache to skip duplicate basins

backlog.spec: Add an alternative start builder. Split the unit square into four quadrants and assign circles to them with counts (7, 6, 7, 6) chosen by a seeded random permutation of the four counts. Inside each quadrant, solve a small max-sum-of-radii problem for its circles, with the quadrant as the container, using the existing _equal_opt on random starts and then _local_opt restricted to that quadrant. Translate the four solved sub-packings back into the full square, shrink them slightly so that they do not overlap across quadrant borders, and then run _local_opt on the combined 26 centres. Use this builder as the start for one restart of run_packing, in place of the lattice start, for k equal to 2 only.
backlog.title: Quadrant decomposition with subproblem solves

backlog.spec: Inside _local_opt, replace the single radius upper bound of 0.5 with a continuation over three stages. In stage one, cap every radius at 0.12 and run the free-radii SLSQP so that the layout must spread over many circles rather than concentrating in a few large ones. In stage two, raise the cap to 0.25 and re-solve. In stage three, remove the cap (use 0.5) and re-solve. Each stage starts from the previous output, and the LP polish and candidate comparison stay as they are. This is a schedule over bounds rather than over a penalty, and it is meant to reach size distributions that the unconstrained SLSQP does not visit from random starts.
backlog.title: Progressive radius-cap continuation

backlog.spec: In jitter_anneal_search and _reinsert_polish, the SLSQP call inside _local_opt currently uses maxiter=300. Make the budget depend on the candidate's quality: run the standard 300-iteration solve first, and if the LP-polished sum is within 0.3 percent of the current best sum, rerun SLSQP from its output with maxiter=1000 and ftol=1e-14 and keep the better result. Candidates further below the best get no extra work. Pass the current best sum into _local_opt as an optional argument, defaulting to None, so the existing call sites still work. This moves compute toward candidates that are close to the incumbent, where small gains are most likely.
backlog.title: Adaptive SLSQP iteration budget for near-best candidates

backlog.spec: In _adam_soft, replace the softplus overlap term with a Huber penetration energy on the overlap o = r_i + r_j - d_ij, using E = 0.5*o^2 for o in (0, delta) and E = delta*(o - 0.5*delta) for larger o, with delta decaying geometrically from 0.2 to 1e-3 over the iterations. Use the same radius-sum reward and the same border terms, with the border overlaps also treated with the Huber form. Derive the analytic gradient for each piece: it is o for the quadratic region and delta for the linear region, multiplied by the usual signs. Keep the Adam learning rate schedule and the final clipping. The Huber form has bounded curvature at large overlap, which may let the early iterations move centres further before the energy stiffens.
backlog.title: Huber-smoothed penetration energy with a decaying delta

backlog.spec: Replace the sequential restart loop in run_packing with a small island model. Run four islands, each with its own seed and its own jitter_anneal_search state, and interleave them in rounds of about 12 seconds each. After each round, each island receives the best packing of its ring neighbour (island i receives from island i-1 mod 4) and replaces its current state with the migrant only if the migrant's sum is larger than its own. Keep a global best with _valid_packing checks as now. The islands keep their own sigma schedules, so migration spreads good basins while preserving diversity. Stop the rounds at the same time budget as the restart loop and then run _reinsert_polish on the global best.
backlog.title: Islands with ring migration of best packings

backlog.spec: Add a constructive start that anchors four circles at the square corners and places the remaining 22 one at a time. For each new circle, choose the candidate point from a seeded set of 2000 uniform samples that maximises the minimum clearance to the already-placed circles and walls, where the clearance of a point is the distance to its nearest neighbour minus that neighbour's current radius, with radii set to the current LP solution after each insertion. Then run _local_opt on the full set. Use this start for one restart of run_packing, alongside the existing LS-growth and lattice starts, and keep whichever final packing is best. The corner anchors are a design choice rather than a learned result, so the greedy growth should fill the interior around them.
backlog.title: Corner-anchored zero-radius start with greedy growth

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform/lattice starts with a clustered seeded start. In a new function _cluster_start(rng), draw k in {3,4,5} cluster centres uniformly in [0.2,0.8]^2, assign the 26 circles to clusters by a seeded multinomial, and place each at its cluster centre plus Gaussian noise with sigma drawn uniformly from [0.05,0.15]. Clip to [0,1], then pass the result through _ls_growth-style pushing (or directly to _local_opt). Use it as the start for every 3rd restart in run_packing, keeping the other starts unchanged, so the search covers clustered basins that the uniform and lattice starts rarely reach.
backlog.title: Gaussian-mixture clustered start

backlog.spec: Add a constructor that builds a packing radius-first. Pick a target radius profile, a seeded geometric sequence from about 0.14 down to about 0.06 over 26 values with a random permutation of which circle gets which target. Visit circles in decreasing target order; for each, place its centre on a 101x101 grid at the point maximising min(border clearance, distance to placed circles minus placed radii minus target radius), using the target radius as the reference size. Feed the resulting centres into _local_opt. Include it as one candidate start in the restart loop, not as the only start.
backlog.title: Greedy decreasing-radius construction

backlog.spec: Add a cheap post-processing step after the final packing is chosen. Scale all centres about (0.5,0.5) by a factor f in [0.97,1.03] (seeded grid of about 25 values, then a golden-section refinement), clip to [0,1], and recompute radii with _lp_radii. Keep the f giving the largest LP sum, and accept it only if _valid_packing passes. This is a one-dimensional exact-feasibility search over the global layout scale that the existing LP step does not explore, and it costs only about 60 LP solves.
backlog.title: Centre dilation line search

backlog.spec: Add a discrete escape move to the search. Every few restarts, take the current best centres and snap a random subset of about 6 circles to a 0.02-spaced grid (seeded), then nudge each snapped circle by a uniform offset of up to 0.01. Re-optimise with _local_opt and keep the result only if the LP sum improves. Because snapping removes the continuous path that the local optimiser follows, it jumps between nearby contact-graph topologies that Gaussian jitter at small sigma rarely crosses.
backlog.title: Quantised-centre tunnelling

backlog.spec: Modify _adam_soft so that it has a time-varying minimum radius. Add a penalty term that pushes every radius above a floor f(t), where f starts at 0.05 and decays linearly to 0 over the iterations, using the existing sigmoid-gradient machinery with a softplus hinge on (f - r_i). The floor forces the optimiser to first find a spread-out, size-diverse configuration and then releases it toward the free optimum. Keep the sum-of-radii term and the schedule of beta and lr unchanged so that only the floor is new.
backlog.title: Radius-floor annealing in the Adam energy

backlog.spec: Inside _local_opt's free-radii stage, replace the uniform objective with a weighted one, sum of w_i r_i. Start with w_i = 1. Run SLSQP, then for each circle compute its relative size s_i = r_i / mean(r) and set w_i <- w_i * exp(0.3 * (1 - s_i)) clipped to [0.5, 2], then re-run SLSQP from the current solution for up to 3 rounds. Finally report the unweighted LP sum of the candidate, so that the weights act only as a path through the space of solutions and the reported score is unbiased. This is a self-adjusting version of the random weight idea, not a fixed one.
backlog.title: Adaptive per-circle pressure weights

backlog.spec: Add an architecture that builds the start in two tiers. Seeded, choose k in {3,4,5} large circles with target radius in [0.14,0.20], placed at random points whose clearance to the border is at least their radius, and keep them fixed while the remaining 26-k small circles are placed by greedy maximum-clearance insertion on a grid. Then run _local_opt on all 26 circles together. This explicitly sets a few large circles in the interior and corners before the small ones fill the gaps, which the existing uniform and lattice starts do not do deliberately.
backlog.title: Two-tier large-then-small seed

backlog.spec: Change run_packing's restart loop to a two-stage allocation. Run 6 seeded short jitter-anneal searches with budget 20 s each, ranking them by LP sum. Then give the remaining wall time, minus a 15 s reserve, only to the top 2 seeds, each continued from its best packing with a fresh jitter-anneal budget. Keep the existing reinsert polish and the validity check. This focuses wall time on the most promising basins instead of spreading it evenly, and it does not change any local solver.
backlog.title: Adaptive restart budget by score rank

backlog.spec: Exploit the fact that SLSQP's path depends on the order of the variables and constraints. In _local_opt, before calling minimize, apply a seeded random permutation p to circle indices (permute the rows of the centres and build I, J from the permuted order), run the constrained optimisation in permuted coordinates, then invert the permutation before calling _lp_radii and the candidate comparison. Use a different permutation for each restart derived from the restart seed. The optimum is identical, but the iteration path differs, which gives cheap extra diversity without any new initialisation.
backlog.title: Index-permutation restarts for SLSQP path diversity

backlog.spec: Add a move that changes the size assignment without moving the centres much. In _reinsert_polish, after the remove-and-reinsert step fails, pick a random pair of circles with radii differing by more than 0.03 and swap their centres (keeping radii as sorted by the LP afterwards), then re-run _local_opt on the swapped layout. Accept the result only on strict improvement of the LP sum and _valid_packing. The move targets the case where the topology is right but big and small circles sit in the wrong places, which the single-circle reinsert cannot fix.
backlog.title: Pairwise-swap-of-sizes move

backlog.spec: After the restart loop, repeatedly pick a random subset of 6 to 10 circles, preferably a spatial cluster around a random centre, and freeze the others. Solve a small SLSQP over the free centres and radii, with the frozen circles as fixed obstacles and their radii as constants. Accept the move only if the full-packing sum (rechecked with _lp_radii and _valid_packing) improves. Run until the deadline, using a fixed seed. This is a large-neighbourhood search that the current single-circle moves do not cover.
backlog.title: Large-neighbourhood subset re-optimisation

backlog.spec: Use scipy.optimize.dual_annealing on the 52 centre coordinates, with bounds [0,1] and a fixed seed. The objective is the negative sum of _lp_radii(centers) for those centres. Cap maxiter and the local-search budget so the call fits in about 60 seconds. Feed the returned centres into _local_opt, and keep the result only if it beats the incumbent. This tests a scipy global annealer that is not yet used in the script.
backlog.title: Global dual-annealing over centres with LP fitness

backlog.spec: Build the initial centres by seeded farthest-point (maximin) sampling. Draw 2000 random candidate points, then greedily select 26 points, each time taking the candidate that maximises its minimum distance to the already chosen points and the square's border. Add a small jitter of about 0.01 and feed the result to _local_opt through jitter_anneal_search as a new start option. This is a data-driven spread-out start, different from the lattice, ring and Vogel starts already tried.
backlog.title: Farthest-point maximin start

backlog.spec: Change the acceptance rule in run_packing so that a restart's result replaces the best-so-far whenever its sum is within a threshold T of the best, not only when it is strictly larger. Set T to start at 0.003 and decay geometrically to 0 across the restarts. Keep a separate true-best record so the returned packing is always the highest-sum valid one. This lets the search drift along a plateau of nearly equal basins before it settles.
backlog.title: Threshold accepting across restarts

backlog.spec: In _adam_soft, replace the clipped wall terms with mirror-image ghost circles. For each centre, add ghost points at (-x, y), (2-x, y), (x, -y) and (x, 2-y), and apply the same softplus overlap energy between each real circle and the ghost of its neighbour's reflection. Keep the existing analytic gradients by reusing the pair formula with mirrored coordinates. Anneal the wall stiffness from soft to hard. The aim is to stop circles from sticking to the clip boundary, which the current hinge-style wall term does.
backlog.title: Ghost-mirror wall repulsion

backlog.spec: At the incumbent packing, form the Hessian of the smooth penalty energy in the centre-and-radius variables, using finite differences of the analytic gradient. Take the eigenvectors with the smallest eigenvalues, which are the nearly flat or saddle directions. Perturb the incumbent by a random combination of the 3 to 5 lowest eigenvectors, scaled to amplitude about 0.02, then run _local_opt from there. Repeat for a fixed number of seeded trials and keep the best valid packing. This uses second-order structure rather than isotropic Gaussian jitter.
backlog.title: Hessian-eigenvector saddle escape

backlog.spec: Run _adam_soft on the same start with a small seeded grid of schedules: initial learning rate in {0.003, 0.01, 0.03}, final learning rate in {1e-5, 1e-4}, and beta from 20 to 1000, 2000 or 4000. Score each run by the post-LP sum, then pass the best two schedules into _local_opt. Fix the grid order and the seed so the result is repeatable, and cap the total time with the perf_counter deadline. This turns the currently hand-set Adam hyperparameters into a small search.
backlog.title: Seeded meta-grid over the Adam schedule

backlog.spec: Before the free-radii SLSQP in _local_opt, solve an LP that first maximises the minimum radius t, subject to r_i >= t for all i, with the pair and border constraints, and then fixes t at 0.98 of its value. Then solve a second LP that maximises the sum of radii under that fixed floor. This places the solution in a more balanced basin before the sum-only objective acts. Use scipy.optimize.linprog with highs, and fall back to the current result if either LP fails.
backlog.title: Lexicographic maximin-then-sum stage

backlog.spec: Build a start from 4 or 5 horizontal strips. Choose the per-strip counts from the integer compositions of 26 whose entries lie in {4,5,6,7}, drawn with a fixed seed. Within each strip, place the circles evenly along x with small random y offsets. Alternate half-offsets between adjacent strips, then pass the result to _local_opt. Keep the best of a small seeded set of compositions. This is a row-based architecture with an explicit count search, which is distinct from the tried ring, hex and pinwheel layouts.
backlog.title: Strip decomposition with per-strip count search

backlog.spec: Keep a list of the best packing at each of the last 5 restart checkpoints. If no restart improves the best sum for 3 consecutive restarts, rewind to the oldest checkpoint and reseed the restart loop from it, with a new seed offset. Otherwise continue as now. Track the rewind count and stop after 2 rewinds, so that the time budget still gets used. This is a stagnation-driven batch policy that the current restart loop does not have.
backlog.title: Checkpoint rewind with stagnation reset

backlog.spec: Before _local_opt, run a short seeded Adam pass on the softplus energy in which every centre also feels a weak attractive pull toward (0.5, 0.5), with strength decaying linearly to zero over the pass. Start from uniform random centres (seed from the restart index). The pull packs the circles into a dense central cluster, and the free relaxation then spreads them to the walls. Keep the existing Adam energy and LP radii; only add the pull term to the centre gradients and set it to zero after the pass. Use it as an alternative start in jitter_anneal_search for about one restart in three.
backlog.title: Gravity compaction start

backlog.spec: Add a basin-escape move to the restart loop. Take the incumbent centres, apply a random seeded affine map (x, y) -> (x + a*y, y*s) with shear a in [-0.3, 0.3] and anisotropic scale s in [0.85, 1.15], then rescale the image so its bounding box fits [0.02, 0.98]^2. Clip the centres into the square and pass them to _local_opt. Accept the result only through the existing best-so-far comparison. The move changes which contacts are active without the Gaussian jitter used elsewhere.
backlog.title: Anisotropic affine shear re-entry move

backlog.spec: Build a packing by growth instead of by removal. Optimise 20 seeded random centres with _local_opt, then insert the remaining 6 one at a time. Each insertion places the new centre at the grid point with the largest clearance (computed as in _reinsert_polish), then runs _local_opt on all current centres. Keep the packing after each step, and use the full 26-circle result as the candidate for the restart loop. Seed the 20-circle start from the restart index so runs are repeatable.
backlog.title: Grow-from-20 incremental insertion

backlog.spec: Add a reheating stage to _adam_soft that starts from the incumbent centres and radii instead of a random start. Run the softplus sharpness beta on a downward-then-upward ladder: drop it from 2000 to 50 over the first 40 percent of iterations, then raise it back to 2000 over the rest. Keep the learning rate as a fixed fraction of the initial rate, around 1e-3. Pass the result through the existing LP radii step and accept it only if the sum improves. Use it inside _reinsert_polish as an alternative move on one attempt in four.
backlog.title: Reverse-beta re-annealing from the incumbent

backlog.spec: Build an alternative start from a seeded Voronoi tessellation. Draw 26 random seed points in the square, and compute the Voronoi vertices with scipy.spatial.Voronoi after reflecting the seeds across the four walls, so the cells stay bounded. Take the 26 vertices closest to the square's centre, or the vertices nearest the 26 seeds, as initial centres, clip them into [0.05, 0.95]^2, and pass them to _local_opt. Use this start in place of the Lubachevsky-Stillinger start for about one restart in four, keeping seeds fixed for repeatability.
backlog.title: Voronoi-vertex seeded start

backlog.spec: Replace the Adam descent on the softplus overlap energy with velocity-Verlet molecular dynamics. Give the 78 variables (26 x, 26 y, 26 r) seeded random initial velocities with small magnitude. At each step compute the analytic gradient of the energy already in _adam_soft, which is the minus-sum-of-radii term plus the sigmoid-weighted penalties. Apply a Nose-Hoover or Berendsen thermostat whose target kinetic energy decays geometrically over the run, so the system cools into a jammed state. Clip to the box and to radius bounds after each step, then pass the result to the LP radii step. This is an optimizer change; keep the Adam path available as a fallback.
backlog.title: Hamiltonian dynamics with a thermostat

backlog.spec: Change the jitter in jitter_anneal_search from Gaussian to heavy-tailed. For each centre draw a Levy-stable step with tail index 1.5 (Mantegna's algorithm, seeded), scaled by the existing sigma schedule from 0.1 down to 0.002. Clip into [0, 1]^2 and call _local_opt as before. Occasional large kicks can jump between basins, while the many small steps still refine the packing. Keep the best-so-far comparison unchanged.
backlog.title: Heavy-tailed Levy-flight kicks

backlog.spec: Add a warp move that maps the incumbent centres through a smooth, non-affine map: x -> x + k*sin(pi*y)*amp and y -> y + k*sin(pi*x)*amp, with k drawn from a seeded uniform in [-0.5, 0.5] and amp in [0.02, 0.08]. Re-clip the centres into the square and run _local_opt on the warped set. Run this move in the restart loop as an alternative to the Gaussian jitter for about one restart in three. The warp keeps the overall layout but moves the contact graph, which is a different kind of perturbation from the existing ones.
backlog.title: Sinusoidal warp of the incumbent

backlog.spec: Build a start with a geometric radius ladder. Choose three tiers with radii a*q^k for k = 0, 1, 2, where a and q are seeded (a in [0.12, 0.16], q in [0.6, 0.8]). Assign counts to the tiers, roughly 4 large, 8 medium and 14 small, summing to 26, with the counts also seeded. Place the circles in order of decreasing tier radius, each at the grid point with the largest clearance from the circles already placed. Then pass the centres to _local_opt, which recomputes the radii. Use the start for about one restart in four.
backlog.title: Radius-ladder tiered start

backlog.spec: Speed up _local_opt and _adam_soft so more restarts fit in the budget. At the start of each call, build the set of pairs whose centres are within 0.35 of each other, plus all border constraints, and pass only those pairs to SLSQP and to the softplus energy. Rebuild the pair set after the first SLSQP iteration batch, and recheck the full set in _valid_packing before accepting any result. Keep the result and the LP radii unchanged, so the only effect should be more restarts per run within the wall-clock limit. Record the number of restarts completed to confirm the speedup.
backlog.title: Cell-list pruned constraints for faster restarts

backlog.spec: Add a seeded start generator _riesz_start(rng) that places 26 centres in [0,1]^2 by minimising a Riesz s-energy, sum over pairs of 1/d^s, plus a boundary image term (each centre also repels its mirror images across the four walls). Begin at s=1 and raise s geometrically to about 12 over 300 L-BFGS-B steps (analytic gradient, centres clipped to [0,1] via bounds). The resulting centres are passed to _local_opt as a restart start, replacing _lattice_start for restart k where k % 3 == 2, and the rest of run_packing stays unchanged. This gives an evenly spread, boundary-aware start that is not a lattice and not a growth process.
backlog.title: Riesz-energy spreading start

backlog.spec: Add _block_cd(c, rng, rounds=40) that alternates over random blocks of 6 to 8 circles. In each round choose a block at random, freeze the other centres and radii as constants, and run SLSQP over the block's centres and all radii with the usual pairwise and boundary constraints. Accept the block update only if the total LP-optimal radius sum rises. Run _block_cd on the output of _local_opt inside _reinsert_polish as an extra candidate, and keep whichever result has the larger sum. Block moves change many coordinates at once without the full-dimensional SLSQP cost.
backlog.title: Random block coordinate descent on centres

backlog.spec: Add _logit_polish(c, r, budget) that maps each centre to the open square with u = logit((x+eps)/(1-x-eps)) so that the box constraints disappear. Build the unconstrained variables u and the radii r (r kept nonnegative via r = softplus(s)). Minimise minus the sum of radii plus a quadratic penalty on pairwise overlap max(0, r_i+r_j-d_ij)^2 and on boundary violations, with an analytic gradient, using scipy L-BFGS-B with a penalty weight raised over 6 stages from 1e2 to 1e7. Finish by calling _lp_radii on the final centres. Run it once on the incumbent at the end of run_packing and keep the result only if it passes _valid_packing and beats the incumbent.
backlog.title: Logit-reparametrised centres for unconstrained L-BFGS polish

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed seed schedule in run_packing with a surrogate loop. Generate 60 candidate starts (mixing _ls_growth, _lattice_start and Riesz-type starts), score each with a cheap proxy (_lp_radii on the raw centres, roughly 0.01 s each), then fit a numpy Gaussian process with a squared-exponential kernel on flattened, sorted-coordinate features of the starts. Use expected improvement over the best proxy score to select the next start for the full _local_opt plus jitter_anneal_search pipeline, refit, and repeat until the time budget is used. Keep the best valid packing as before. Only numpy is used, with a Cholesky solve and a small nugget for stability.
backlog.title: Gaussian-process surrogate for choosing restart seeds

backlog.spec: Add _apollonian_start(rng) that builds a start by recursive corner filling. Begin with four circles of radius about 0.2 placed in the square's corners. Repeatedly take the largest empty corner-like gap, which is the point of the current packing with the greatest clearance to the walls and to existing circles, and place a new circle there at the clearance radius times a random factor in [0.8, 1.0]. Continue until 26 circles are placed, then pass the centres to _local_opt. Use the seed rng so the process is repeatable. This is a hierarchical, multi-scale start built from the boundary inward, unlike the grid, ring, hex or growth starts already tried.
backlog.title: Apollonian-style recursive corner filling start

backlog.spec: Add _aspect_detour(c0, rng) that optimises the packing inside a rectangle of width w and height h = 1/w, not the unit square, with w swept from 0.8 to 1.25 over 6 stages. At each stage run the existing _adam_soft or SLSQP step with the boundary constraints using those bounds, warm-starting from the previous stage. Finally map the centres back to the unit square by an affine rescale and recompute radii with _lp_radii, which is always valid. Use the detour output as an extra candidate in _local_opt next to the existing candidates. The idea is to let the packing reorganise across container shapes, which may escape square-specific basins.
backlog.title: Aspect-ratio detour homotopy

backlog.spec: Add _match_average(A, B) that takes two elite packings with centres A and B (each 26x2 with radii), solves a minimum-cost assignment between their centres using scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment on pairwise distances, and averages each matched pair of centres, with weights proportional to each packing's score. The averaged centres form a new start for _local_opt. Keep the best three packings from the restart loop as the elite set and, after the restart loop, generate three averaged starts from its pairs. Keep a result only if it beats the incumbent. This is a permutation-aware recombination, unlike cut-and-splice crossover.
backlog.title: Hungarian-matched elite averaging

backlog.spec: Add _contact_lp(centres, r) that finds the set of pairs with gap below 0.02 times the mean radius and, for only those pairs plus boundary contacts, linearises the constraints around the current centres. It then solves a linear program for the centre step and radius step within a trust-region box of width delta, using scipy linprog with highs. Accept the step only if the true sum of _lp_radii rises. Shrink delta by half on rejection and grow it by 1.5 on acceptance, for at most 80 iterations. Call _contact_lp inside _reinsert_polish on the best packing. This uses the contact graph to restrict the linearisation, which keeps the LP small.
backlog.title: Trust-region LP on contact-graph subsets

backlog.spec: In _local_opt, after the free-radii SLSQP, run a ratchet loop of 30 rounds. Each round draws a random cap vector: the radius bound of each circle is set to its current radius plus a uniform value in [0, 0.01], and the bounds are used in an SLSQP solve on centres and radii with the usual pairwise constraints. Accept the result if the sum rises, otherwise keep the previous packing. The ratchet is monotone, so it can only improve, and it lets smaller circles grow when neighbours shift. Use a fixed seed derived from the centres so runs are repeatable.
backlog.title: Randomised radius-cap ratchet

backlog.spec: Add a soft prior to the Adam softplus energy in _adam_soft that encodes a shell profile: for each circle, a target radius that is a decreasing function of its distance from the square's centre, with the largest target near the centre (for example target_i = a - b*dist_to_centre_i with a and b fixed). Add a quadratic term lambda*(r_i - target_i)^2 whose weight lambda is annealed from 0.05 to 0 across the iterations, with analytic gradients added to the existing gr vector. Use this only for the even-indexed restarts, to diversify which size pattern the optimiser reaches. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Shell-by-shell radius profile prior

backlog.spec: In _adam_soft, replace the softplus overlap term with a soft-sphere ratio penalty. For each pair, use q_ij = (r_i + r_j) / dist_ij and penalise max(0, q_ij - 1)^2 with a smooth surrogate; keep the same border terms. Anneal the exponent p of a power-law energy sum((r_i+r_j)^p / d_ij^p) from p=8 up to p=200 over the Adam iterations, with the hinge applied after the last stage. Keep the analytic gradients (chain rule through d_ij^p and the ratio), and keep the LP polish and SLSQP candidates unchanged so the final packing is still validated by _valid_packing.
backlog.title: Soft-sphere ratio penalty with exponent annealing

backlog.spec: Add a stage after _local_opt. Alternate two steps for about 30 rounds: (a) given centres, solve the LP for radii as now; (b) take target radii equal to the LP radii scaled up by a factor 1.02, and relax the centres by minimising the total squared pair and border overlap with L-BFGS-B, using analytic gradients over the centres only. After each round, rerun the LP on the relaxed centres and keep the best valid sum seen. Stop when the sum no longer improves for 5 rounds. This is a pump that moves centres toward feasibility for slightly larger radii, and it is not a penalty continuation in the standard sense.
backlog.title: Feasibility-pump alternation between LP radii and target-radius relaxation

backlog.spec: In _adam_soft, at each iteration keep a random 40 percent subset of the pair overlap terms (seeded generator, per-iteration draw), scaling their gradients by 1/0.4 so the expectation is unchanged. Keep all border terms active. Anneal the keep probability from 0.4 back to 1.0 over the last third of iterations so the final steps see the full energy. This injects gradient noise that can move centres out of shallow basins without a separate perturbation loop.
backlog.title: Stochastic constraint dropout in the Adam energy

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform growth rate in _ls_growth with per-circle multipliers drawn once from a seeded lognormal distribution (sigma 0.5). Each circle grows its radius at rate*m_i per step, with the same decay of the global rate. Keep the pairwise push-apart loop and the boundary clipping. Use the resulting centres as the start for jitter_anneal_search in the first restart only. The goal is to let small and large circles jam in different places, which the homogeneous growth tends to prevent.
backlog.title: Heterogeneous-rate growth start

backlog.spec: In run_packing, replace the fixed sequence of restart starts with a bandit over four start generators: random LS growth, perturbed lattice, farthest-point maximin, and the incumbent with a Gaussian kick. Each arm starts with one pull. After each restart, record the arm's reward as the improvement over the previous best sum, or zero. Select the next arm with a UCB score mean + 0.5*sqrt(log(t)/pulls), using a seeded generator for ties. Keep the time budget, best-so-far tracking and final reinsert polish as they are.
backlog.title: UCB bandit over start generators

backlog.spec: Raise total_budget in run_packing to about 225 s and move the reinsert deadline to t_start + 245 s, so the job still ends before the 5-minute kill with margin. Add a guard in jitter_anneal_search and _reinsert_polish that checks elapsed time before each _local_opt call and stops if fewer than 6 s remain before the deadline. Keep the valid-packing check on the final result. This is a schedule change only: it makes the restart loop use the wall-time budget that is currently left unused.
backlog.title: Full-budget schedule with wall-clock guard

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 1e-10 shrink in _lp_radii with an exact final rescale of the returned packing. Compute the largest factor f in (0, 1] such that f times every radius satisfies all border and pair constraints in double precision, using the ratio of the tightest constraint, then multiply all radii by f times (1 - 4e-16). Check the result with _valid_packing and fall back to the 1e-10 shrink if the check fails. This recovers the small loss from the fixed margin without risking an invalid packing.
backlog.title: Exact-feasibility final rescale

backlog.spec: Add a seeded start generator _cosine_grid_start(rng) that builds a 6x5 tensor grid whose coordinates follow a cosine spacing, x_i = 0.5 - 0.5*cos(pi*(i+0.5)/6) for x and the analogous 5-point cosine spacing for y, so points crowd toward the walls. Keep 26 of the 30 points by dropping 4 at random with rng.choice, add uniform jitter of amplitude 0.02 with rng, and clip to [0,1]. In run_packing, use this generator for restart indices k where k % 3 == 2, in place of _lattice_start for those restarts. Leave all other code unchanged.
backlog.title: Cosine-spaced tensor-grid start

backlog.spec: Add _checker_start(rng) that places 26 seed centres on a 6x5 lattice with 4 random sites removed, as in _lattice_start, and assigns each seed an initial radius of 0.09 on checkerboard-even sites and 0.06 on odd sites. Pass these radii through a seeded jitter of plus or minus 10 percent. Feed the centres to _local_opt as usual, since its LP stage recomputes all radii anyway. Use this start for restart k where k % 4 == 3. The change only alters the initial centre layout and should not modify the reinsert or LP logic.
backlog.title: Two-size checkerboard seed

backlog.spec: In _adam_soft, replace the Cartesian centre variables with polar coordinates about the square centre (0.5, 0.5): store rho and theta per circle, with x = 0.5 + rho*cos(theta) and y = 0.5 + rho*sin(theta). Compute the softplus gradients with respect to x and y as before, then apply the chain rule to get gradients for rho and theta. Initialise rho from the distance of each start centre to (0.5, 0.5) and theta from its angle, then clip rho so each centre stays inside the square after conversion. Return Cartesian centres with the same clipping as the current code. Keep the radii variables and the Adam schedule unchanged.
backlog.title: Polar parametrisation of centres in the Adam energy

backlog.spec: In _local_opt, after the first LP on the warm-start centres, identify rattlers as circles whose LP shadow prices for all their border and pair constraints are zero (within 1e-9). Freeze the rattlers at their current positions and run the free-radii SLSQP only on the remaining jammed circles, building the pair and border constraints only for index pairs among the jammed set plus the frozen circles' fixed contributions. Afterwards put the rattlers back and take the LP radii over all circles. This shrinks the SLSQP problem and frees budget for more restarts in run_packing. Keep the candidate-selection logic so the final choice is still by LP sum.
backlog.title: Rattler-freezing reduced SLSQP

backlog.spec: In _local_opt's free-radii SLSQP, add a spread term to the objective that rewards the minimum pairwise centre distance: obj(z) = -sum(r) - lam * t, with a new auxiliary variable t bounded above by every pairwise distance, t <= sqrt(dx^2+dy^2) written as the constraint dx^2+dy^2 - t^2 >= 0. Set lam = 0.02 for the first call and decay it by factor 0.5 per restart index k in run_packing, so the bonus vanishes after a few restarts. The last SLSQP solve in each call must use lam = 0 so the final sum of radii is the true objective. Add the matching gradient entries for t.
backlog.title: Decaying centre-spread bonus in the SLSQP objective

backlog.spec: In jitter_anneal_search, track the number of consecutive iterations without improving best_s. When this count reaches 5, reset the perturbation scale to sigma = 0.05 (a reheat) and restart the geometric decay from that value over the remaining iterations, so the decay goes from 0.05 to 0.002. Reset the stagnation counter after each reheat. Leave the random seed and perturbation draws otherwise unchanged, so the search remains reproducible. Keep the total iteration count K = 20 and the time-budget check.
backlog.title: Stagnation-triggered sigma reheating in the jitter chain

backlog.spec: In _local_opt, reparametrise the free-radii SLSQP variables as z = [x/s, y/s, r/s] with s = 0.1, so coordinates and radii are O(1) and the pair and border constraint gradients are better conditioned. Set bounds to [0, 1/s] for centres and [0, 0.5/s] for radii, pass the scaled constraints, and unscale the result before the LP polish. Raise maxiter to 500 and try ftol 1e-14. Keep the candidate list and the final LP selection unchanged.
backlog.title: Variable scaling and tighter tolerance for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Replace the single SLSQP maximisation in _equal_opt with a bisection on a shared radius s. For each trial s, minimise a squared-overlap penalty over the 52 centre coordinates using L-BFGS-B, starting from the previous feasible centres. Declare s feasible if the penalty falls below 1e-14, and bisect 25 times between 0.05 and 0.11. Return the centres from the largest feasible s, then pass them to the existing free-radii stage unchanged.
backlog.title: Equal-radius feasibility bisection warm start

backlog.spec: In jitter_anneal_search, scale each circle's Gaussian kick by its local clearance instead of using one sigma for all circles. Compute clearance_i as the LP radius of circle i in the current best packing, normalised to mean 1. Use sigma_i = sigma * clip(clearance_i, 0.5, 2). Circles with slack get larger kicks and tightly jammed circles get smaller ones. The sigma schedule itself stays the same.
backlog.title: Clearance-scaled perturbation of centres

backlog.spec: In jitter_anneal_search, accept a candidate whose sum of radii is within 1e-7 of the current best even when it is not strictly larger, and move the current state to it. Keep best_c and best_r tied to the strict maximum. This lets the chain drift across equal-score plateaus, which are common among rattler-containing packings, without changing the perturbation schedule or the restart loop.
backlog.title: Plateau-drift acceptance in the jitter chain

backlog.spec: In _adam_soft, use two learning-rate schedules: a centre rate that decays from 0.01 to 1e-4 as before, and a radius rate that decays from 0.003 to 3e-5 with the same geometric form. Apply them through a per-coordinate lr vector built each step. Leave the softplus energy, the beta annealing and the clipping unchanged.
backlog.title: Separate learning rates for centres and radii in the Adam energy

backlog.spec: In _local_opt, add a proximal term lambda * ||z - z_ref||^2 to the free-radii SLSQP objective, where z_ref is the start point and lambda = 1e-3. This keeps each local solve near its basin and reduces jumps between basins during jitter steps. Run a second pass with lambda = 0 from the regularised solution, then take the LP polish as before. Only the objective and its gradient change.
backlog.title: Proximal-regularised SLSQP local step

backlog.spec: In _adam_soft, evaluate the softplus gradient at a look-ahead point z + beta1 * m before the usual Adam update, and keep the bias-corrected second-moment estimate as is. This is a Nesterov-style variant of the existing Adam step. Keep the annealed beta, the learning-rate schedule and the final clipping unchanged so the change is isolated.
backlog.title: Nesterov momentum in the Adam softplus energy

backlog.spec: Add a restart seed built from the best packing. Rotate all centres about (0.5, 0.5) by a seeded angle drawn uniformly from [-0.15, 0.15] radians. Affinely rescale the rotated points by a factor below 1 so they stay inside [0.05, 0.95]^2, then clip. Pass the result to _local_opt. This moves the packing relative to the walls, which the existing sinusoidal warp and shear moves do not do. Use it for about one restart in four.
backlog.title: Rotate-and-refit kick

backlog.spec: In _adam_soft, clip each centre update to a maximum displacement d_t per step, where d_t decays geometrically from 0.02 to 0.0005 over the iterations. Apply the clip after the Adam step and before the box clipping. The radii keep their current update. This keeps early steps from jumping across the square and late steps from oscillating, without changing the softplus energy.
backlog.title: Per-step displacement trust region in the Adam energy
