backlog.spec: In _local_opt, run a first SLSQP pass with the objective sum_i w_i * r_i, where w_i = 1 + eps * (distance of centre i from the square centre), eps = 0.05. Anneal eps linearly to 0 over two stages, re-solving from the previous solution each time, and finish with the unweighted objective. The LP polish then ranks the candidates as before. This is a close variant of the rejected objective-weight randomisation, with the tilt annealed instead of seeded.
backlog.title: Position-tilted objective annealing

backlog.spec: Add a seeded start generator that first optimises the 26 centres and radii on a flat torus, where pair distances use the minimum-image convention and radii are capped at 0.5. Use the same Adam softplus energy but drop the wall terms. After convergence, map centres into [0,1]^2 by a seeded random affine scaling that keeps them inside, then hand the result to _local_opt as the start. Use this start only for restart k=2 and k=5 of run_packing so that the incumbent path is untouched.
backlog.title: Toroidal periodic-start relaxation

backlog.spec: Add a stage in which the wall-touching structure is fixed before the free-radii SLSQP. Choose a seeded integer vector (for example 4 circles touching the bottom, 4 the top, 4 the left and 4 the right, drawn from the current incumbent by nearest-wall rank). Replace the inequality wall constraints for those circles with equalities x_i = r_i, 1-x_i = r_i, y_i = r_i or 1-y_i = r_i, solve SLSQP over centres and radii, then release the equalities and run the normal _local_opt. Keep the result only if the LP-scored sum improves.
backlog.title: Prescribed wall-contact counts as SLSQP equalities

backlog.spec: Add a move to jitter_anneal_search. Choose a random line through the square, sample a seeded direction and offset, and select the circles on one side of the line. Reflect those centres across the line and clip to [0,1]. Then call _local_opt on the result, with the centres of the other side left untouched. Use this move on roughly one iteration in four, alternating with the existing Gaussian jitter, and accept by the usual LP-scored sum comparison.
backlog.title: Cluster reflection across a random line

backlog.spec: Add a start generator built from spectral embedding. Create a seeded random sparse graph on 26 nodes (each node connected to its 4 nearest nodes in a random 2D point set). Form the graph Laplacian, take the eigenvectors for the 2nd and 3rd smallest eigenvalues, and use them as the x and y coordinates. Rescale to [0.08, 0.92] with a small seeded jitter. Pass the result to _local_opt. Use it as a restart start for k=3 and k=7 only, so that the usual restarts are kept.
backlog.title: Laplacian-eigenmap spectral start

backlog.spec: Add an alternative radius update to _adam_soft. Keep the centres updated by Adam, but optimise the radii in log space with a multiplicative (mirror-descent) step: log r <- log r + eta * g_r * r, followed by a clip to the border cap. Use an eta that decays geometrically from 0.05 to 0.001 over the iterations. Once the centres have converged, finish with the existing LP radii for the final centres. Compare the LP sum with the incumbent and keep whichever is larger.
backlog.title: Mirror-descent on log-radii

backlog.spec: Add a bank of all local optima found in jitter_anneal_search and the restart loop, storing each as a contact-graph signature (sorted list of touching pairs with rounding to 1e-3). For each new restart, sample 30 seeded random candidate starts, compute each candidate's distance in signature space to the bank, and pick the one farthest from all stored signatures as the start. Otherwise keep the existing run_packing structure unchanged, so that the restart budget and best-so-far tracking stay the same.
backlog.title: Novelty-driven restart seeding

backlog.spec: Change the perturbation in jitter_anneal_search so the kick magnitude is not uniform. After each _local_opt call, compute the LP dual values for the pair and wall constraints of the current best packing. Give each circle a stress score equal to the sum of its active duals. Perturb each centre with a Gaussian whose scale is proportional to its normalised stress score, so that highly stressed circles move more and rattlers stay put. Keep the existing sigma schedule as the overall scale.
backlog.title: Stress-guided perturbation

backlog.spec: Add a combinatorial local search over centres discretised to a 1/160 lattice inside [0.05,0.95]^2. Start from the incumbent centres rounded to the lattice. At each step pick a random circle and try the 8 neighbouring lattice points plus 8 random lattice points within 0.1. Score each candidate with _lp_radii (fixed centres, LP sum), accept only improvements, and stop after a fixed number of evaluations seeded from a fixed generator. Use the best discrete packing as the input to _local_opt, and keep it only if the final LP sum exceeds the incumbent.
backlog.title: Integer-lattice discrete local search

backlog.spec: Add a start built from the elite packings already visited. Collect the best 5 packings from the restart loop, sort the radii of each in decreasing order, and average the sorted radii across the elites. Fit a linear map from the sorted rank index to radius using least squares. For a new start, assign each circle a seeded random position in the square and an initial radius from this fitted profile, then run _adam_soft from those radii before _local_opt. Use this start for one restart only, so that the rest of the run is unchanged.
backlog.title: Data-driven radius prior from elite packings

backlog.spec: Replace the final SLSQP stage in _local_opt with a BFGS run on an exact L1 penalty merit function over centres and radii. The merit is minus the sum of radii plus a penalty mu times the sum of positive parts of the pair and wall violations. Choose mu from 10 to 1000 geometrically, running scipy minimize with method BFGS at each mu. Use the existing analytic-style vectorised violations and their subgradients. Compare the LP-scored sum with the SLSQP candidate and keep the better one.
backlog.title: BFGS on an exact-penalty merit function

backlog.spec: Add a seeded hard-disk Monte Carlo stage before _local_opt. Start from random centres with small radii. Repeat many sweeps: propose a random move of one centre by a step size that adapts toward about 40 percent acceptance, and accept it only if no overlap or wall violation results at the current radii. Every sweep, also propose a box-compression move that scales all radii up by a small factor, accepted if the configuration stays feasible. Compress until acceptance collapses, then pass the centres to _local_opt. Keep the existing pipeline unchanged apart from this new start generator.
backlog.title: Hard-disk Monte Carlo pressure compression

backlog.spec: In _local_opt-style optimisation, first solve the packing inside a superellipse container |x-0.5|^p + |y-0.5|^p <= 0.5^p with p starting at 8 and decreasing geometrically to 2, then map the result into the square with p=2 and no clipping. Use the standard softplus energy or SLSQP with the wall constraints replaced by the superellipse constraint. The goal is that corner regions are filled differently before the square walls are enforced. Run it as an alternative start for one restart in the restart loop, keeping the best valid packing as before.
backlog.title: Superellipse container homotopy

backlog.spec: Replace the isotropic Gaussian kick in jitter_anneal_search with a kick restricted to a random low-dimensional subspace. Each iteration draws k in {4,...,8} random orthonormal directions in the 52-dimensional centre space (seeded), and moves the centres only along those directions with an amplitude drawn from the existing sigma schedule. Then run _local_opt on the perturbed centres and accept if the LP sum improves. This explores coordinated large moves that isotropic noise rarely produces, while leaving the rest of the search unchanged.
backlog.title: Random-subspace basin hopping

backlog.spec: Before the restart loop, generate 1500 seeded random centre sets (uniform, or perturbed lattice) and score each one by the LP radii from _lp_radii, which is cheap compared with SLSQP. Keep the 8 highest-scoring sets and run _local_opt on each, instead of running a single random start per restart. Feed the best of these into the existing restart loop as its first start. The screening uses only the existing LP and seeded randomness, so the result stays repeatable.
backlog.title: LP-screened start pool

backlog.spec: Add a projection-based optimiser for the packing. Given fixed radii that are the current LP radii scaled up by 1.02, alternate between (a) projecting each overlapping pair of centres apart along their line of centres by half the overlap, and (b) clipping each circle so it lies within its wall margin. Run until the maximum violation is below 1e-9 or 2000 sweeps. Then recompute the LP radii for the resulting centres. Use this as an extra candidate inside _local_opt's candidate list, so it can only help when it gives a larger LP sum.
backlog.title: Alternating projections between overlap and wall sets

backlog.spec: Add a seeded start built from a hexagonal lattice patch of 26 points with one vacancy and one interstitial. Choose the lattice spacing and orientation at random within a fixed range, place a hexagonal patch of roughly 27 points centred in the square, delete one point nearest a random location, and insert one point at the largest-clearance position in the patch. Clip the centres into [0.05, 0.95] before passing them to _local_opt. Use this start in one restart slot of the existing restart loop, keeping the others unchanged.
backlog.title: Lattice-defect start

backlog.spec: In _adam_soft, replace the Adam update for the centre and radius variables with a sign-momentum update (Lion style): the step is lr times the sign of an exponentially averaged gradient, with momentum 0.9 and decoupled weight decay of 1e-4 applied to the radii. Keep the existing beta annealing and learning-rate decay. Leave the clipping to the boxes unchanged. This changes only the optimiser geometry of the same energy, so it can reach different basins at the same iteration count.
backlog.title: Signed-gradient update on the softplus energy

backlog.spec: In _local_opt's free-radii SLSQP stage, add a small reward on the objective for pairs whose gap is below 2e-3 after the first solve, so the solver is nudged toward rigid contact networks with more active constraints. Implement it as a second SLSQP pass with objective minus lambda times the sum of the number of pairs with gap below the threshold, with lambda set to 1e-3, and then run a final pass with lambda equal to zero. Keep the best candidate by the LP sum as the code already does.
backlog.title: Contact-count bonus in the free-radii SLSQP

backlog.spec: After the first LP solve in _local_opt, read the dual values of the pair and wall constraints. Use them to set per-circle target radii that are proportional to the sum of the duals of each circle's active constraints, normalised so the targets sum to the LP sum. Solve SLSQP with the objective being the squared distance of the radii from these targets with a weight of 0.1, plus the normal sum-of-radii term with weight 1. This biases the radii toward the stress-consistent profile before the final free-radii solve, and it is a one-line change in spirit to the existing two-phase schedule.
backlog.title: Shrinking-target radius profile from the LP dual

backlog.spec: Start from an arbitrary centre set and a uniform small radius. Alternate between growing all radii by a factor of 1.001 and pushing overlapping pairs apart with the projection step, then clip to the walls, with the growth factor decreasing each cycle as 1 minus 1e-3 times cycle over 600 cycles. Once growth stalls, run _lp_radii and then the usual _local_opt. This keeps the jamming dynamics of the Lubachevsky-Stillinger start but uses a multiplicative schedule on all radii at once instead of additive per-circle rates, giving a different jamming order.
backlog.title: Jam-then-relax with gradual wall restoration

backlog.spec: In jitter_anneal_search, replace the fixed geometric sigma schedule with a success-rate controller. Track accepted steps over a sliding window of 5 perturbations. If more than 1/5 of recent kicks improved best_s, multiply sigma by 1.15; otherwise multiply it by 0.87. Clamp sigma to [0.002, 0.1]. Keep the seeded rng and the existing time budget. The rest of the chain is unchanged.
backlog.title: 1/5 success-rule adaptive jitter sigma

backlog.spec: In _reinsert_polish, the insertion point is still the argmax of a 51x51 grid clearance. Keep the grid argmax as a starting point, then take the top 5 grid points by clearance and refine each with scipy.optimize.minimize (Nelder-Mead, xatol 1e-6, maxfev 200) on the clearance function min(border(p), min_j(|p - c_j| - r_j)), negated. Insert the best refined point, which may be off-grid, and run _local_opt as before. Accept the move under the same sum-improvement and _valid_packing rule.
backlog.title: Continuous refinement of the reinsertion hole

backlog.spec: In _reinsert_polish, instead of running _local_opt on the single argmax insertion point, rank the top 8 well-separated grid candidates by the sum from _lp_radii on the kept centres plus the candidate point (a cheap LP only). Run the full _local_opt only on the best 2 by LP sum. Keep the best result under the existing acceptance rule. Use a fixed candidate separation of 0.08 so the 8 candidates are distinct holes.
backlog.title: Two-stage hole screening before full local optimisation

backlog.spec: _lp_radii maximises the plain sum of radii, which is degenerate, so many optimal radius vectors exist and the choice is arbitrary. Add a tiny secondary objective: maximise sum(r) + 1e-7 * sum(w_i r_i), where w_i = 1 - 2*dist(c_i, (0.5, 0.5)) / sqrt(2) for the interior circles. This steers ties toward large circles at the centre. Keep the primary value unchanged up to the tiny weight, and keep the validity check and the 1e-10 shrink.
backlog.title: LP degeneracy tie-break with a centrality weight

backlog.spec: In _local_opt, after the equal-radius phase, run the free-radii SLSQP three times more, each from the same centres but with radii initialised as the LP radii multiplied by independent uniform draws in [0.85, 1.0] per circle (seeded from a fixed generator). Add each result to the candidates list before the final LP-score selection. This widens radius-basin coverage without changing the centres or the acceptance rule.
backlog.title: Multi-start free-radii SLSQP from random radius draws

backlog.spec: Add a perturbation move to jitter_anneal_search that is local rather than global. With probability 0.25 per kick, choose a random disc of radius 0.25 to 0.35 centred on a random circle centre. Rotate every centre inside that disc about the disc centre by a random angle in [-0.5, 0.5] radians, then clip to the square. The other kicks are unchanged. Use the seeded rng and pass the result through _local_opt as usual.
backlog.title: Random disc rotation kick

backlog.spec: In _lattice_start, the 4 dropped grid points are chosen at random. Replace that with a seeded greedy rule: start from the full 5x6 grid, repeatedly drop the grid point whose removal costs the least minimum pairwise spacing among the remaining points, breaking ties with the rng, until 26 remain. Then apply the existing jitter amplitude. This keeps the lattice flavour while choosing a better-spread keep-set.
backlog.title: Restart seeds from the four quadrant-maximin drop rule

backlog.spec: In jitter_anneal_search, scale the Gaussian kick of each circle by its LP-radius slack, defined as its LP radius over the mean LP radius, clipped to [0.5, 2]. Small circles (rattlers) get larger kicks so they can move to new holes, and large circles get smaller kicks. The global sigma schedule is unchanged. Compute the LP radii once per accepted step, not per kick.
backlog.title: Radius-adaptive jitter by LP slack

backlog.spec: In run_packing, after each restart, record the gap between the best and second-best restart sums. If the gap is below 2e-4 (the restarts agree), reserve the remaining budget for _reinsert_polish with a 1.5x longer deadline. Otherwise start another restart as now. The total deadline stays at 235 s so the wall-time margin is kept. This is a budget-allocation change only, with no change to the search operators.
backlog.title: Time-split between restart search and reinsertion by score gap

backlog.spec: After _reinsert_polish returns, build a 101x101 grid over the unit square and compute the clearance of each point against the final centres and radii. Take the 3 largest-clearance points that are at least 0.1 apart. For each, try inserting a circle there after removing the smallest-radius circle, run _local_opt on the new 26 centres, and keep any result that beats the incumbent sum and passes _valid_packing. Stop after about 15 s of wall time.
backlog.title: Final polish on a 101-point grid around the largest holes

incumbent.description: Adds a perturbed-lattice start (5x6 grid, 4 random points dropped to leave 26, jitter amplitude cycled over 0.01 to 0.1 across restarts) for restarts k>=1, keeping the LS-growth start for k=0, and keeps the best valid packing as before.
